## Hypothesis

The sniper_real_fills_grinder top keeper (SNIPER_VIX18_GRINDER) exhibits negative edge on walk-forward out-of-sample and real-fills validation, confirming that the apparent in-sample edge is an artifact of overfitting to a specific VIX regime and exit mechanics.

## Mechanism

The candidate uses SNIPER_LEVEL_BREAK entries with VIX>=18 and a VIX-trend regime filter (VIX > 5-day average), exiting via profit_lock_threshold=0.0 (artifact) and a fixed runner mechanism. Walk-forward OOS splits the 16-month OPRA dataset into expanding windows; real-fills validation replays the same logic against cached OPRA bid/ask with slippage model.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline P&L.
2. **Sample bias:** Sample = all sniper_real_fills_grinder combos that passed initial filters (n=432). Selection method = top keeper by in-sample wide_pnl. Overfit risk = high due to grinder size and lack of OOS filter during selection.
3. **Out-of-sample:** WF=0.173 (VIX18 best case) -- fails WF>=0.70 gate. Walk-forward OOS negative across 4/4 most-recent months.
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (real OPRA replay shows -$3,291 OOS vs IS $24,537; diff -113%).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day = -$1,200 (single-day loss); max drawdown = -$9,482 (Nov-Dec 2025 + Jan 2026); blow-up scenario = prolonged low-VIX trending market where level breaks fail to hold.
6. **Concentration:** Top-5 days = 120% of P&L (IS); OOS top-5 days = 210% of P&L (indicating extreme instability).
